"On-call pages 85→22/week — over what time period, and is that company-wide or your team's rotation?"
"ferry — did you write it, or take it over as maintainer later? When was '1.2k stars' true?"
"Is anything of Kestrel Freight's or Lumen Pay's internal architecture, dashboards, or systems off-limits to show, even in outline?"
No question or claim about its fate; the only mention is "I've read everything in material/ — your resume, LinkedIn text, and old 2019 site."

invented.claim: Soak caption asserts nothing has gone wrong since: "For 40 teams, and for ferry's maintainers since 2022, it hasn't" — no such outcome is in the material or in what the person said.
Concept B proposes showing "the two sub-ten-minute incidents ... and how they were recovered" — how they were recovered was never stated (unchosen concept).

final.question: What makes a migration boring on the day?
final.form: His own migration runbook, in its own stage names: preflight, shadow, dual write, cutover, soak, decommission
final.object: Plain stencilled steel shipping containers, five to twelve of them

swap.reason: It rests on this person's own runbook stage names, a freight employer's containers and "the trucks kept running," the 2014 library table, and ferry's cutover command — none of which transfer to another platform engineer unchanged.

backdrop.reason: The pieces carry the content itself — crates crossing toward 310, one container relabelling 11→15, two shakes for the two incidents, stacks snapping into one — not ambience behind text.

depth.reason: Seven chapters run in a causal order where decommission and soak only make sense after cutover, opening on one closed container and closing on the whole set.

clipart.reason: The object is a shipping container tied to the freight employer, explicitly chosen over the SRE stock emblems of server racks and dashboards.

honesty.reason: The plan replaces "zero downtime" with 99.98% plus the two internal incidents, says "we" for the pages figure, credits ferry's creator, and holds Lumen Pay to one line; only the Soak caption's "it hasn't" overreaches slightly.

thirty_seconds.reason: The opening screen gives name and the question, and a fixed rail with a permanent "Close" item jumps straight to the answer, a visible number, email and CV without scrolling.

plain_reader.reason: "What makes a migration boring on the day?" is plain English to an outsider and is the exact professional value an insider would respect.

judgement.summary: A single-scroll 3D page structured as the person's own migration runbook — preflight through decommission — with stencilled shipping containers as one object that restacks, relabels and flips to numbers at each stage, answering "What makes a migration boring on the day?" and closing on an invitation to write. Its greatest weakness is that it leans entirely on built-from-nothing visuals with no real artifact to show, and a few captions (notably the Soak beat's claim that nothing has gone wrong for 40 teams or for ferry since 2022) stretch past what the person actually said.
